article_text:
東京都江戸東京博物館（東京都墨田区）で、江戸東京博物館リニューアル記念特別展「円山応挙 リアルの先へ 空間革命」が11月28日から開催されます。

江戸時代、絵画はかつてない広がりと豊かさを見せ、多彩な様相を呈しました。伝統と革新が交錯するなか、円山応挙（1733～1795）は、自然の姿を丹念に観察し、確かな筆致によって、写生にもとづいた独自の画風を生み出しました。しかし、応挙の「写生」は、対象の形を的確に捉えるだけにとどまりません。生き物の気配や光の移ろいにまで目を向けた表現は、従来の絵画に新たな広がりをもたらしました。その画風は多くの門人に受け継がれ、日本美術に大きな影響を与えました。

さらに応挙は、空間全体を一つの世界として構成する絵画にも取り組みました。その代表が兵庫県香美町・亀居山大乗寺（通称「応挙寺」）に伝わる「孔雀の間」、「芭蕉の間」、「山水の間」の障壁画です。部屋ごとに画題や構図が綿密に計画され、襖や壁面が連続して独自の空間を生み出すこれらの作品は、応挙芸術の到達点として高く評価されています。

本展では、応挙が手掛けた大乗寺障壁画を中心に、初期から晩年に至る画業をたどります。写生にもとづく描写に加え、作品の装飾性や広がりのある空間表現に注目し、応挙芸術の魅力と革新性について紹介されます。

江戸東京博物館リニューアル記念特別展 「円山応挙 リアルの先へ 空間革命」

会場：東京都江戸東京博物館 1階特別展示室（東京都墨田区横網1-4-1）

会期：2026年11月28日（土）～2027年1月24日（日） ［前期展示］11/28（土）～12/24（木） ［後期展示］1/2（土）～24（日） ※会期中、一部の作品は上記以外にも展示替えあり

開館時間：午前9時30分～午後5時30分 ※土曜日は午後7時30分まで （入館は閉館の30分前まで）

休館日：月曜日（ただし1/4、11は開館）、12/25（金）～1/1（金）、1/12（火）

アクセス： JR総武線「両国駅」西口から徒歩3分 都営地下鉄大江戸線「両国駅」A3・A4出口から徒歩1分

詳細は、 展覧会公式サイト まで。

展覧会の見どころ

見どころ① 応挙芸術の全貌に迫る 約20年ぶりの大規模回顧展

120点を超える応挙作品が一堂に集結します。初期の眼鏡絵から晩年の大乗寺障壁画まで、多彩な作品を通して応挙の画業が総合的に紹介されます。

見どころ② 応挙が仕掛けた空間革命 大乗寺障壁画を体感する

大乗寺に伝わる実物の障壁画とともに、「孔雀の間」、「芭蕉の間」、「山水の間」の空間を再現。絵画と空間が響き合う世界をご体感ください。

見どころ③ 初公開、里帰り作品も 応挙、再発見

初めて公開される「 牽牛花図 」。イギリスからはセインズベリー視覚芸術センター所蔵の「虎図」が、久しぶりに日本へ里帰りします。新たな出会いと、時を経た再会。応挙の多彩な表現が、ここに広がります。

展覧会構成

第1章 絵師応挙の誕生（～1766）

若き日の応挙は、「主水」「一嘯」「夏雲」「仙嶺」など、時期に応じて複数の名を用いました。狩野探幽の流れを汲む石田幽汀に学ぶ一方、当時流行した沈南蘋の画風なども学びました。さらに眼鏡絵の制作を通じて培った遠近表現は、のちに応挙が独自の空間表現を築くうえで重要な基盤となります。

第2章 明和 明和3～9年（1766～72）

応挙が「応挙」と名乗るのは明和3年（1766）34歳の夏からです。以後、「応挙之印」、「仲選」の印章とともに、この名を生涯使い続けました。この時期に大きな影響を与えたのが、円満院門主の祐常でした。祐常との交流は、応挙が写生へ向かう一つの契機となり、祐常が日常の諸事万端を書き留めた「萬誌」には応挙の言葉も書き留められています。

第3章 安永 安永元～10年（1772～81）

祐常との交流を通して貴族社会とのつながりを得た応挙は、安永期には三井家をはじめとする京都の上層町人からの支持を集めました。三井家の依頼による「郭子儀祝賀図」や、親しい関係をうかがわせる「夕涼み図」などが残されています。また、40歳を迎えた頃から屏風のような大作も増えていきました。安永4年（1775）版の「平安人物志」では画家の筆頭に名が掲げられ、京を代表する絵師として存在感を高めていきます。

第4章 天明 天明元～9年（1781～89）

天明期、応挙は名実ともに京を代表する絵師となり、各地の寺社で障壁画を次々と手がけました。愛知の明眼院、和歌山の草堂寺と無量寺、香川の金刀比羅宮、兵庫の大乗寺などに、大画面を生かした作品を残しています。複数の部屋を飾る障壁画の制作には、一貫した構想のもとで門人たちをまとめる力が必要でした。こうした大規模な制作は、円山派が画派として形を整えていたことも示しています。国宝「雪松図屏風」などの傑作が生まれた一方、天明8年（1788）の大火で応挙も被災しました。

第5章 寛政 寛政元～7年（1789～95）

天明の大火後に始まった御所造営では、土佐派や狩野派などの絵師とともに、応挙も一門を率いて障壁画制作に参加しました。当時の障壁画は嘉永7年（1854）の火災で失われましたが、その制作過程を伝える下絵が残されています。御所の仕事を終えた応挙は、大火によって中断していた大乗寺の障壁画を完成させました。晩年まで大画面と向き合い、最期まで新たな空間表現を追い求めました。

自然の綿密な観察から生まれた「写生」を極め、さらには部屋全体をひとつの世界として構築するダイナミックな「空間革命」へと到達した円山応挙。約20年ぶりの大規模回顧展となる本展では、初期の貴重な眼鏡絵から円熟期を象徴する国宝「雪松図屏風」、初公開作、そしてイギリスからの里帰り作まで、120点を超える傑作が一堂に会します。なかでも兵庫・大乗寺に伝わる名高い障壁画群の実物と、展示室内に創出される立体的な空間再現の体感展示は、応挙が仕掛けた空間芸術の真髄を全身で味わえる圧倒的なハイライトとなるでしょう。リニューアルオープンを経て、より没入感を増した同館の特別展示室で、巨匠の革新的な美の世界を存分に体感してみてはいかがでしょうか。（美術展ナビ）

article_text:
Lightdox has acquired world sales rights to “The Big Boom!,” the latest documentary from Swiss filmmaker Gabriel Tejedor, ahead of its world premiere in IDFA ’s Frontlight program.

The film explores the contradictions of a Bulgarian town pulled into Europe’s shifting geopolitical order, where arms production for Ukraine’s frontlines collides with enduring ties to Russia, personal convictions, and the everyday need to survive.

Related Stories

Lara Croft’s Inaugural Voice Actor Shelley Blond Recalls First Time She Saw ‘Tomb Raider’ Character: ‘I Thought She Was Very Sexy and Very Ballsy’

In Kazanlak, known as Bulgaria’s “Valley of Roses,” rose oil production and folklore traditions exist alongside a major arms industry. The Arsenal factory, the town’s main employer, provides work for thousands of people manufacturing weapons and ammunition. Through the lives of four residents, Tejedor examines the place this industry occupies in the town’s economy and identity, and the questions it raises for those whose lives depend on it.

Popular on Variety

“I have never been interested in war or weapons. But the invasion of Ukraine shattered my convictions,” Tejedor said. “Ever since, one question has haunted me: what does it mean to be a pacifist today? I do not judge the workers at Arsenal, nor the local population.

“ ‘The Big Boom!’ does not seek to lecture, but to confront the gray zones of a continent trapped in its own paradoxes.”

Anna Berthollet, CEO of Lightdox, said, “‘The Big Boom!’ brings us face to face with a contradiction at the heart of today’s Europe – a town making the weapons of war while struggling with its own loyalties and beliefs.

“Gabriel Tejedor finds a way into this reality that feels both clear-eyed and deeply human. As someone of Bulgarian origin myself, I find his sensitive portrayal of Kazanlak and its people particularly meaningful. He reveals the layers of history, identity and geopolitical influence that shape the region without reducing them to a political argument.”

Tejedor is a Swiss filmmaker and journalist whose work explores utopias and the relationship between individuals and authority across the former Soviet Union and its satellite states.

“The Big Boom!” is his fifth feature film, following “Rue Mayskaya” (selected for Visions du Réel and IDFA) and “Kombinat” (selected for Visions du Réel).

“The Big Boom!” is produced by Mira Film Basel GmbH, and is co-produced by RTS Radio Télévision Suisse and SRG SSR, with the support of Swiss and regional film funds and cultural institutions.

title_original: Patrick Stewart, stage and ‘Star Trek’, ‘X-Men’ star, dies at 86
editorial_title_zh: 帕特里克·斯图尔特（Patrick Stewart），舞台剧与《星际迷航》、《X战警》明星逝世，享年86岁
editorial_excerpt_zh: 这位经古典训练的演员在洛杉矶逝世。

"斯图尔特的银幕首作出现在1970年代，包括限定剧集《我，克劳迪斯》和《锅匠，裁缝，士兵，间谍》。他最受赞誉的工作是出演《星际迷航：下一代》剧集中企业号星舰舰长让-吕克·皮卡尔，该剧自1987年播出至1994年。斯图尔特在四部故事片中再次饰演了该角色。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Stewart was born in Mirfield in what is now West Yorkshire on July 13, 1940, to a textile worker and an Army sergeant major."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "He joined the Royal Shakespeare Company in the 1960s and first appeared on Broadway in a production of A Midsummer Night’s Dream in 1971. Source: Wiki Commons / Maximilian Bühn CC BY-SA 4.0

Patrick Stewart

Patrick Stewart, the UK actor who achieved fame on stage and the silver screen and whose credits included the Star Trek and X-Men films, has died. He was 86.

A excerpt from a statement posted to Stewart’s Instagram account read: “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday [October 28] at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.”

The statement added, “His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre. He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.”

Stewart was born in Mirfield in what is now West Yorkshire on July 13, 1940, to a textile worker and an Army sergeant major.

He joined the Royal Shakespeare Company in the 1960s and first appeared on Broadway in a production of A Midsummer Night’s Dream in 1971. He won the Laurence Olivier Award for supporting role in Antony And Cleopatra in London’s West End in 1979, and would win his second in 2009 for portraying Claudius in Hamlet , a role that garnered a Tony Award nomination for the Broadway version.

Stewart’s first screen roles came in the 1970s and included limited series I, Claudius, and Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy . His most celebrated work came when Stewart landed the role of the Starship Enterprise captain Jean-Luc Picard in the Star Trek: The Next Generation series that ran from 1987 to 1994. Stewart reprised the role in four features.

The innate decency of Picard appealed to Stewart, who appreciated the same sense of integrity in Charles Xavier aka Professor X, the leader of the X-Men franchise that saw him star from 2000 to 2017 in the core franchise and spin-offs like Logan , for which he earned a Critics Choice award supporting actor nomination.

Notable film credits included John Boorman’s celebrated 1981 fantasy epic Excalibur and Jeremy Saulnier’s 2015 psychological thriller Green Room , in which he played against type as the leader of a white supremacist group. His last credit was for voice work in Working Title’s whodunnit The Sheep Detectives , which opened this year. Stewart reprised his role as Xavier in Marvel Studios’ upcoming Avengers: Doomsday , which is scheduled to open on December 18.

He was married three times, most recently to the musician Sunny Ozell. He is survived by Ozell and his children Daniel and Sophia from his marriage to choreographer Sheila Falconer.

Stewart was knighted in 2010.

Tributes

William Shatner , who first played Captain Kirk in the original television series Star Trek: “What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor. From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work.”

Ian McKellen , who acted with Stewart in the X-Men films and on stage in Waiting For Godot and No Man’s Land :

“Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end. You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love.”

Hugh Jackman from the X-Men franchise:

“We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days.”

Rebecca Romijn from the X-Men franchise:

“I just heard the very sad news about the passing of my dear friend Patrick Stewart. I feel so grateful to have known him for the last 25 years, and to have been in his orbit for the last 25 years, both as a fellow mutant and as a fellow member of Starfleet.”

Famke Janssen from the X-Men and Star Trek franchises: “Patrick was a legend. One of the greats. I had the pleasure and honour of working with him over several decades. First as Kamala opposite him as Captain Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and later on as Jean Grey with Patrick embodying Professor X in the X-Men movies. You will be missed, Patrick, but never forgotten.”

The Royal Shakespeare Company:

“We are deeply saddened to hear of the passing of RSC Honorary Associate Artist, Sir Patrick Stewart; a colossus of both stage and screen and one of the finest classical Shakespearean actors of his generation.”

Trevor Roth , COO of Star Trek: The Final Frontier executive producers Roddenberry Entertainment: ”To say that we are heartbroken is an understatement. When Patrick Stewart entered the franchise he had a tough job ahead of him. It was not only his talent but his moral fortitude that allowed audiences to embrace a new generation of captain — one that chose diplomacy over aggression and showed that standing up for others is always the right choice. Today we have lost not only a captain on screen, but a leader in life. Our hearts go out to his family, friends, and fans throughout the world.”

article_text:
Drei Jahre lang konnte man einmal im Monat kostenlos in viele Berliner Museen. Dann wurde das Angebot wegen Sparmaßnahmen gestrichen. Jetzt sieht das Sondierungspapier von Linke, Grünen und SPD eine Wiedereinführung vor

Kann man vielleicht künftig wieder regelmäßig an Sonntagen kostenlos ins Museum? Vier Wochen nach der Wahl zum Berliner Abgeordnetenhaus haben sich Linke, Grüne und SPD auf ein Sondierungspapier geeinigt, das Grundlage für die nun folgenden Koalitionsverhandlungen ist. Darin wird auch die Wiedereinführung der 16 kostenlosen Museumssonntage pro Jahr und der Kulturkarte für Jugendliche geplant. "Der Zugang zu Kunst, Musik, Theater und Museen darf nicht vom Einkommen der Eltern abhängen", heißt es in der nun vorgelegten Grundlage für Sondierungsgespräche.

Der eintrittsfreie Museumssonntag war 2024 wegen Einsparungen im Kulturhaushalt weggefallen. Einmal pro Monat konnte man seit 2021 viele Häuser in der Hauptstadt besuchen, ohne Eintritt zu zahlen. Insgesamt nutzten mehr als 2,2 Millionen Menschen das Angebot.

Der Museumssonntag war eines der Vorhaben, die von Kulturprojekte Berlin organisiert wurden. Die landeseigene Gesellschaft, die vor 20 Jahren gegründet wurde, plant etwa auch die Art Week, die Lange Nacht der Museen und historische Jubiläen, zuletzt auch die Silvesterparty am Brandenburger Tor.

article_text:
It’s likely the case that there were tens of thousands of short films released into the world this year. (Sundance alone fielded 11,153 short-film submissions.) Naturally, the reader will expect the author of this superlative list to have watched all of them. While that is far from the case, he can honestly claim to have watched hundreds—and certainly at least 10 that are worth your time, and which don’t require much of it. As ever, the following, in no particular order, are proof that brevity poses no limit to cinematic potency.

Caring Cabin (Chelsea McMullan and Douglas Nayler Jr., 12 min)

Prior to receiving a dementia diagnosis, trans icon and singer-songwriter Beverly Glenn-Copeland was in the process of creating a children’s show conceived by his partner Elizabeth Copeland. This glimpse at the project radiates with all the healing energy of Glenn-Copeland’s otherworldly music.

Morning Circle (Basma al-Sharif, 21 min)

The dreariness of exile gives way to hope for the next generation in Berlin-based Palestinian filmmaker al-Sharif’s disarmingly joyful new work.

An Impossible Address (Suneil Sanzgiri, 38 min)

A reflection on the life and legacy of Angolan revolutionary Sita Valles raises the specters of 20th-century Afro-Asian solidarity; the struggle for independence from colonialism; and the painful, enduring complexities of what comes after.

All Said Done (Micah Weber, 22 min)

An intimate interview with the filmmaker’s father forms the core of this abstract masterpiece, which Weber calls “an incomplete image of class relations and affective labor.”

Remote Views (Alexis McCrimmon, 15 min)

A mesmerizing found-footage film transmitting images of Black life as broadcast on television in ’80s America.

Tuktuit (Caribou) (Lindsay McIntyre, 15 min)

Using her own hand-processed celluloid made from caribou skin, McIntyre visualizes the Inuit relationship to land, lichen, and animal life.

We Were the Scenery (Christopher Radcliff, 15 min)

A young couple flee Vietnam and find themselves as extras on the set of Francis Ford Coppola’s Apocalypse Now ; years later, they recount the experience.

Fiction Contract (Carolyn Lazard, 10 min)

A birthing simulation plays out with all the emotional stakes of the real thing, raising visceral questions about race, gender, object- and personhood, care, surveillance, and reality.

Carol & Joy (Nathan Silver, 39 min)

Silver’s moving documentary about actress Carol Kane and her mother Joy sits in the tradition of great interview films like Portrait of Jason , Numéro zero , and American Boy: A Profile of Steven Prince .

Tessitura (Lydia Cornett and Brit Fryer, 18 min)

An elegant profile of three trans opera singers that conveys the art form’s ecstasy and rebuts conservative assumptions about its nature.

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在阿拉伯语中，“fidai”意为甘愿为更大利益自我牺牲的人。巴勒斯坦电影人卡马尔·阿尔贾法里在他的拼贴电影中借用了这个有时在军事语境下使用的词，策划了一场强有力的影像起义，以对抗宣传和历史抹去的浪潮。影片的大部分内容取材于曾存放于贝鲁特巴勒斯坦研究中心（Palestine Research Centre）的档案材料。1982年，在黎巴嫩内战期间，以色列军队突袭了该中心并查封了这批档案。这批关于巴勒斯坦历史的大多数文件——书籍、报纸、视听文物——据信目前仍掌握在以色列军队手中。", "links": [{"text": "Palestine", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/world/palestinian-territories"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "通过秘密渠道获得、在阿尔贾法里这部电影中重见天日的镜头，带有政治压制的物理痕迹。这些影像布满划痕、颗粒感十足且像素化，但通过蒙太奇的力量，它们唤起了令人震惊的视觉平行呼应，指向巴勒斯坦人数十年间经受的持续暴力。英国委任统治时期拍摄的黑白电影显示，士兵们在街道上巡逻并对本土居民施加暴力；随后以色列军队也犯下了类似行径。剪辑没有采用时间顺序，而是通过重复出现的影像构建了一种延续性。一次又一次，我们看到了被拆毁的房屋、受惊吓的儿童以及被占领军杀害的巴勒斯坦人的尸体。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部电影不仅是一部汇编作品，还进行了自身的历史干预。许多片盘上都印有以色列当局添加的贬损性说明，阿尔贾法里用红漆条将其覆盖。取而代之的是加桑·卡纳法尼（Ghassan Kanafani）等巴勒斯坦作家的诗歌节选，这些文字将一种人性重新赋予了这些过去的影像。通过这些收复与挽救的策略，阿尔贾法里的电影为这座被囚禁的档案库带来了解放，哪怕只是暂时的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "电影", "links": [{"text": "Film", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/film"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "纪录片", "links": [{"text": "Documentary films", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/documentary"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "巴勒斯坦", "links": [{"text": "Palestine", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/world/palestinian-territories"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "黎巴嫩", "links": [{"text": "Lebanon", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/world/lebanon"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "以色列", "links": [{"text": "Israel", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/world/israel"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "中东与北非", "links": [{"text": "Middle East and north Africa", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/world/middleeast"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "影评", "links": [{"text": "reviews", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/tone/reviews"}], "translated": true}]

article_text:
I n Arabic, “fidai” means someone willing to sacrifice themselves for the greater good. Borrowing this word, which is at times used in a military context, for his collage film, Palestinian film-maker Kamal Aljafari stages a potent uprising of images against the tide of propaganda and historical erasure. Much of the film draws on archive materials once housed in the Palestine Research Centre in Beirut. In 1982, during the Lebanese civil war, Israeli forces raided the centre and seized the archive. Most of these documents on Palestinian history – books, newspapers, audiovisual artefacts – are believed to still be in the hands of the Israeli army.

Obtained through clandestine means, the footage that resurfaces in Aljafari’s film bears the physical traces of political suppression. The images are scratched, grainy and pixelated, yet through the power of montage they evoke startling visual parallels that point to the relentless violence endured by Palestinians through the decades. Black-and-white film taken during the British mandate show soldiers patrolling the streets and inflicting violence upon the Indigenous population; similar acts then committed by Israeli forces. In place of a chronological order, the editing builds a sense of continuity through recurring images. Time and time again, we see torn-down houses, terrorised children and the bodies of Palestinians murdered by occupation forces.

More than simply a work of compilation, the film also performs its own historical intervention. Many of the reels are imprinted with pejorative captions added by Israeli authorities, which Aljafari covers in streaks of red paint. In their place are excerpts from poems by Palestinian authors such as Ghassan Kanafani, whose words return a sense of humanity to these past images. Through these strategies of reclamation, Aljafari’s film brings liberation, if only momentarily, to a captive archive.
